message.content:
The Declaration of Independence was signed by 56 delegates from the Thirteen Colonies. Some of the most well‑known signers include:

| Signer | State | Role |
|--------|-------|------|
| John Hancock | Massachusetts | President of the Continental Congress |
| Thomas Jefferson | Virginia | Principal author of the draft |
| Benjamin Franklin | Pennsylvania | Senior statesman and diplomat |
| John Adams | Massachusetts | Future Vice President and President |
| Samuel Adams | Massachusetts | Revolutionary leader |
| George Washington | Virginia | Commander-in-Chief of the Continental Army |
| Patrick Henry | Virginia | Famous orator (“Give me liberty, or give me death!”) |
| James Madison | Virginia | Future “Father of the Constitution” |
| Alexander Hamilton | New York | Future Secretary of Treasury |
| John Jay | New York | Future Chief Justice of the Supreme Court |

Other notable signers include:

- **Robert R. Livingston** (New York)
- **John Witherspoon** (New Jersey)
- **George Wythe** (Virginia)
- **William Paca** (Maryland)
- **Thomas Stone** (Maryland)
- **George Clymer** (Pennsylvania)
- **James Smith** (Pennsylvania)
- **John Penn** (Pennsylvania)
- **John Dickinson** (Delaware)
- **George Read** (Delaware)
- **John Taylor** (Delaware)
- **George Ross** (Pennsylvania)
- **John Hart** (New Jersey)
- **William Livingston** (New Jersey)
- **John McCausland** (New Jersey)
- **John Rutledge** (South Carolina)
- **Charles Pinckney** (South Carolina)
- **Edward Rutledge** (South Carolina)
- **John Rutledge** (South Carolina)
- **John Hancock** (Massachusetts)

(For a complete list, you can refer to the official records of the Continental Congress.)
